features.name: Sandbox prerequisite handling — explicit, non-passing UNSUPPORTED outcome when user-namespace isolation is unavailable (NDEBT-043)
features.description: Maintenance tranche (H-PHASE-014 fold; first, because 104 depends on it). tools/test_convergent_review.py probes the HOST capability directly (`unshare --user --map-root-user true`), independent of tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh, before the five sandbox-dependent tests. When isolation is unavailable each of those tests is reported with the token UNSUPPORTED on its own result line (an explicit unittest skip whose reason starts 'UNSUPPORTED: user-namespace isolation unavailable'), the run prints a 'CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL' line, and the process exits NON-ZERO (required-conformance mode is the default — the documented 'required gate' command never passes on a host that cannot prove isolation). The new flag --allow-unsupported-isolation (local development only; CI never passes it) turns that same outcome into exit 0 while still printing every UNSUPPORTED line and 'CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL'. On an isolation-capable host the tests execute and the run prints 'CONFORMANCE: FULL'. The flag never masks any other failure. tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh and tools/isolated_trial_adapter.py are NOT modified (the fail-closed sandbox is never weakened, and the suite never runs a trial unsandboxed). tools/README.md's Machine Validation section documents the flag and both conformance outcomes. CAPABLE-HOST EVIDENCE OBLIGATION: AT1, AT2 and AT4 are host-conditional; the operator workstation restricts user namespaces, so only their restricted-host branches run here. The capable-host branches are discharged in CI by feature 104: 104 AT5/AT6 (the required-mode job prints 'CONFORMANCE: FULL' with no skips = AT1's capable branch) and 104 AT7/AT8 (a throwaway branch applying exactly AT4's isolation-removal mutation, i.e. both of AT4's replacements: the unshare namespace line in tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh and the Landlock restrict-self call in tools/isolated_trial_adapter.py, makes the job fail on test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network with 'AssertionError: 40 != 0', the cross-trial secret read = AT4's capable branch). KNOWN LIMIT (NDEBT-046): no test in the suite detects the loss of the namespace half on its own. Removing only the unshare line leaves all 54 tests passing, because Landlock still enforces the file leg and the network leg accepts any OSError (ECONNREFUSED included); so AT4 proves that removing isolation is detected, through the filesystem leg. Making the sandbox tests discriminate the namespaces is outside 103's scope. AT2's capable branch is additionally run by the Evaluator wherever isolation is available, and otherwise recorded as not exercised. Polarity note: NIP-0003 sketches the opposite polarity (--require-isolation opt-in) for its own future suite; this feature sets the framework precedent (required by default), recorded for the NIP-0003 pre-acceptance revision in docs/planning/backlog_reconciliation.md.
